title: 20 Airbnb Guest Review Examples and Templates for Hosts (2026)
summary: 20 Airbnb guest review templates for ideal, messy, late and rule-breaking stays, plus Airbnb's review rules, dispute steps and PMS automation.
body_markdown:
A good Airbnb guest review runs one to three sentences, names one concrete detail from the stay, and comes with star ratings for cleanliness, communication and house rules. The 20 guest review templates below are grouped by guest type, followed by Airbnb's review policies and automation tools.


## How do hosts review guests on Airbnb?


Airbnb hosts review guests within 14 days of checkout by submitting a public written review alongside 1-to-5-star ratings in three categories: cleanliness, house rules, and communication ([Airbnb Help](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/3287) ). Airbnb combines those three scores into an averaged rating for the stay. Leaving a review is optional, but a host who submits ratings must also write the public text. Neither side sees the other's review until both are in or the 14 days end. If you submit first, you can edit yours anytime within the 14-day period until the guest submits theirs ([Airbnb Help](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/367) ).


Guest star ratings are not shown on a guest's public profile. A host sees a guest's detailed and averaged ratings only when that guest requests or books a stay, and Airbnb uses them for Instant Book and experienced-guest eligibility and to enforce its ground rules for guests ([Airbnb Help](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/3287) ). They sit alongside the other checks in[Airbnb guest screening](https://www.conduit.ai/blog/airbnb-guest-screening) .


During the review you can tick optional "what you did well" highlights (kept the place neat and tidy, took care of garbage, sent helpful messages, was respectful, always responded) and add a private note that only the guest and Airbnb can read. A low rating in any category prompts you to say what didn't go well, and future hosts see that feedback next to a warning icon (same page). After publication you have 30 days to remove a review you wrote ([Airbnb Help](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/3582) ), and once it is removed you cannot write a new one for that stay ([Airbnb Help](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/2673) ). For reviews written from the guest side, see these[Airbnb review examples to leave for your host](https://www.conduit.ai/blog/airbnb-review-examples-for-hosts) .


## What should a host write in a guest review?


A useful guest review tells the next host one specific thing about how this guest treated the home and its rules, because that host will read it when deciding whether to accept a booking.[Airbnb's hosting guidance](https://www.airbnb.com/resources/hosting-homes/a/why-reviews-matter-41) suggests a line of thanks, a concrete detail ("This guest followed our checkout instructions perfectly") and raising sensitive issues by direct message. Avoid pasting one identical review for every guest.[Guesty's help page](https://help.guesty.com/hc/en-gb/articles/19737140337949-Setting-auto-reviews-for-Airbnb-and-Vrbo) warns that using the same template for many reviews can affect your Airbnb ranking, and future hosts reading ten copies of the same sentence learn nothing about the guest.


Judge the stay against a normal turnover. Scattered towels or an unmade bed are part of routine cleaning and do not justify a negative review; your[Airbnb cleaning checklist](https://www.conduit.ai/blog/the-ultimate-airbnb-cleaning-checklist-for-hosts) already budgets for them, and a family with small children will leave more of that than a solo traveler. Unreported broken items, smoking indoors against house rules, and neighbor noise complaints are fair, factual details to include.


A specific detail makes a positive review more useful to the next host than general praise. Compare these two:


- Weak review: "Great guest, everything was fine. Would host again."
- Useful review: "Maya kept the kitchen tidy all week and locked up on time at checkout. We would happily host her again."


## What are good Airbnb review examples for an ideal guest?


Ideal guest reviews name one habit that made hosting easy, such as sending an arrival time, keeping common rooms tidy or respecting quiet hours, and end with a recommendation to other hosts. A specific behavior next to a 5-star score gives the next host something to go on when the booking request arrives. The six templates below cover families, couples, work trips, long stays, groups and a first stay with you; replace` \[Guest name\]` and change the detail to match the stay.


1. "\[Guest name\] and their two kids were a pleasure to host. They told us their arrival time a day ahead and left the toys packed away in the bin we provide. Any host would be glad to have this family."
2. "Easy, friendly guests. \[Guest name\] and their partner gathered the used towels and locked up at 11 on the dot."
3. "\[Guest name\] stayed for a work week and left the desk and kitchen as they found them. When the building's elevator was out on Tuesday, they messaged us before we had heard about it. Recommended."
4. "Hosting \[Guest name\] for a month was easy. They put the bins out on collection day without being reminded, and we found the place in great shape at checkout."
5. "Six friends, zero noise complaints. \[Guest name\]'s group kept to the guest count on the booking and wound down before our 10 p.m. quiet hours."
6. "This was \[Guest name\]'s first stay with us, and they read the house manual before arriving: every question they sent was one the manual didn't cover. Welcome back anytime."


## How do you review a guest who left the place messy?


Reviewing a messy guest means separating routine turnover clutter from a mess that required excessive or deep cleaning. Under Airbnb's[ground rules for guests](https://www.airbnb.com/resources/hosting-homes/a/ground-rules-for-guests-554) , guests must not leave a home in need of deep or excessive cleaning, such as carpets soiled by pets. When cleanup goes past a normal turnover, rate cleanliness accurately and describe the condition calmly without guessing intent. The four templates below keep the wording factual.


1. "The home needed a deep clean after \[Guest name\]'s stay. Food spills had dried on the counters and stovetop, and our cleaner needed two extra hours."
2. "\[Guest name\] left trash in several rooms, and a red wine spill on the living room rug needed professional stain treatment. Future hosts should expect extra cleanup."
3. "\[Guest name\] was polite in messages. The unit, though, needed far more than a normal turnover: sticky residue on most surfaces and unbagged trash in the kitchen and living room."
4. "Because of the state of the kitchen and both bathrooms, our cleaner could not finish before the next check-in, and the arriving guests waited 40 minutes. We would not host \[Guest name\] again."


## How do you review a guest who broke a house rule?


A house-rule complaint in a guest review is fair when the rule is one of Airbnb's seven standard house rules (maximum guests, quiet hours, events, pets, smoking, commercial photography, and locking up at checkout) or another rule shown in your listing's house rules section when the guest booked ([Airbnb ground rules](https://www.airbnb.com/resources/hosting-homes/a/ground-rules-for-guests-554) ). For bookings made on or after November 20, 2026, Airbnb generally does not let hosts require stripping beds, taking trash offsite, or washing and putting away dishes, does not allow hosts to fine or penalize guests, and does not allow new rules added after booking through messages or posted signs ([Airbnb Help](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/4168) ). Do not mark a guest down for skipping those tasks. When a guest breaks a rule that was listed, name the rule and what it caused, as these four do.


1. "\[Guest name\] had extra people stay overnight who were not on the reservation, which put the house over its listed maximum. They left it tidy, but other hosts may want to confirm the full guest count before check-in."
2. "The home smelled strongly of smoke after \[Guest name\] checked out, and our listing is non-smoking. We had to air it out and deep clean before the next guests arrived."
3. "\[Guest name\] brought a dog even though our listing says no pets. They were polite about it, and we needed an extra cleaning after checkout."
4. "Neighbors complained about a loud gathering past our 10 p.m. quiet hours during \[Guest name\]'s stay. Events are not allowed at our home, so we would not host this group again."


## How do you review a guest who checked out late without asking?


Late checkout reviews work best when they give the time the guest left and what it did to the turnover, in a flat tone. An unapproved late departure eats into the hours a cleaner has before the next check-in. Note whether the guest answered your checkout reminder and whether the rest of the stay went well, then set the communication or house rules rating to match.


1. "\[Guest name\] left the home in good condition but checked out at 12:15, more than an hour after our 11:00 checkout, without asking for an extension. Our cleaning schedule for the next guests slipped as a result."
2. "Our cleaner waited outside for 90 minutes on checkout day because \[Guest name\] had not left and did not answer our morning reminder."
3. "A smooth stay until departure day, when \[Guest name\] left at 1 p.m., two hours after checkout, without asking. Our cleaner had two fewer hours to get the home ready for the next guests."


## How do you review a guest with communication problems?


Communication problems are worth a review when they changed the stay for you or the next guest, for example a late arrival nobody was told about. Hosts depend on replies to arrange check-in and to fix things during a stay. Say what was missing and how it affected the stay, and give the communication rating that matches, as in templates 18 to 20.


1. "We had no arrival time from \[Guest name\] and no reply to our check-in messages, so nobody was ready when they arrived at 11 p.m. and getting them inside took half an hour. They left the place in fair shape."
2. "\[Guest name\] did not answer our messages about a scheduled pool service, so the technician could not get in and had to come back the next day. The home was left neat."
3. "The home was clean, but \[Guest name\] did not mention a broken lamp during the stay, and our cleaner found it after checkout. Hearing about it sooner would have let us replace it before the next guest."


## How do you write a fair negative review of a guest?


A fair negative review of a guest tells future hosts what happened without breaking Airbnb's content rules or turning a small annoyance into a permanent mark on the guest's profile. Write every sentence as if you might have to show Airbnb Support the evidence for it. Before you submit, go through these six steps:


1. Check the facts against your listed house rules and booking details before writing.
2. Describe what happened during the stay rather than characterizing the guest's personality.
3. Leave out names of other people, your property address, and any personal information.
4. Put coaching for minor habits in the private note so a generally good guest can improve without hurting their future bookings.
5. Rate the specific category that matches the problem (cleanliness, communication, or house rules) instead of dropping all three scores automatically.
6. Report serious violations to Airbnb Support as well as writing the review, as outlined in Airbnb's[ground rules for guests](https://www.airbnb.com/resources/hosting-homes/a/ground-rules-for-guests-554) .


When a guest was fine overall but could do one small thing better, the private note is the place for it:


- "Thanks again for staying with us, \[Guest name\]. Next time, please share an estimated arrival window the day before so check-in goes smoothly."
- "We enjoyed hosting you, \[Guest name\]. A quick heads-up for future trips: wet towels left on wooden benches can mark the finish, so hanging them in the bathroom helps protect the furniture."
- "Glad you had a good trip, \[Guest name\]. If you ever need extra time on checkout morning, send a message ahead so we can coordinate with our cleaner."


## What does Airbnb's content policy allow in a guest review?


Airbnb's content and review policies allow honest, first-hand facts about a stay and prohibit reviews that are abusive, disclose private information, or are incentivized or retaliatory. Under Airbnb's[Content Policy](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/546) , public reviews and private notes cannot contain discriminatory, harassing, threatening, demeaning, or insulting content, cannot publicly disclose another person's private information, and cannot be spam or content shared repeatedly in a disruptive manner. The policy covers content generated or edited with AI as well.[Hospitable's help page](https://help.hospitable.com/en/articles/4559914-automate-your-airbnb-reviews-using-review-rules) adds that Airbnb does not allow URLs, email addresses, or phone numbers in reviews.


Airbnb's[Reviews Policy](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/2673) further prohibits irrelevant, fake, competitive, and incentivized or pressured reviews. Hosts and guests cannot give or withhold a review in exchange for something, including informal trades such as offering 5 stars if the other side leaves 5 stars. Airbnb does not remove a review only because someone disagrees with the star rating or with an opinion in it, so keep the review to facts from the stay.


## What can a host do about a retaliatory guest review?


Hosts can dispute a retaliatory guest review through Airbnb when a guest leaves a negative review after the host reports a serious violation such as property damage, an overstay, a house rule violation, or an unauthorized party ([Airbnb Resource Center](https://www.airbnb.com/resources/hosting-homes/a/how-to-dispute-retaliatory-reviews-552) ). Airbnb usually decides a removal request within 48 hours and allows up to two removal requests per review ([Airbnb Help](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/3582) ).


To support a dispute, submit evidence such as photos and Airbnb message threads proving both that a serious policy violation happened and that reporting it to Airbnb or the guest likely led to the review. Keep all guest communication inside Airbnb Messages so Support can verify the timeline directly. If the guest's negative review points to something that did go wrong, such as a dirty shower or a broken lock, it is not retaliation; fix it before the next arrival and say so in your public reply.


## How do hosts automate guest reviews and review reminders?


Property management software automates guest reviews by posting a 5-star review a set number of days after checkout, picking from saved templates filled with the guest's name and listing details. Set up once, it works like scheduled[Airbnb automated messages](https://www.conduit.ai/blog/airbnb-automated-messages-how-to-automate-your-guest-communication) , and you still write the reviews for problem stays yourself. The table compares Hostaway, Guesty, Hospitable and OwnerRez from each vendor's own help pages.


Tool When it posts Template rotation Edit or skip a review


[Hostaway](https://support.hostaway.com/hc/en-us/articles/360060848813-Host-Reviews-Auto-reviews) 1 to 13 days after checkout (Airbnb and Vrbo) Minimum 3 templates picked at random; variables` {{guest_first_name}}` ,` {{listing_name}}` Edit or cancel scheduled reviews


[Guesty](https://help.guesty.com/hc/en-gb/articles/19737140337949-Setting-auto-reviews-for-Airbnb-and-Vrbo) Midnight the day after checkout, with optional delay (Airbnb and Vrbo) Unlimited Airbnb templates picked at random; variables` {{guest}}` ,` {{guest_first}}` ,` {{listing_address_city}}` Stop auto-review for a specific reservation


[Hospitable](https://help.hospitable.com/en/articles/4559914-automate-your-airbnb-reviews-using-review-rules) You set the timing; Hospitable recommends 3+ days after checkout (Airbnb only) Multiple review rules, one picked at random Edit text and each category rating before publishing; a negative review can be held until the last possible moment


[OwnerRez](https://www.ownerrez.com/support/articles/reviews-automatic-posting-5-star-airbnb) On by default; 5 days after departure unless you change the wait (Airbnb and Vrbo) Rotates between as many templates as you create (Airbnb only; Vrbo has no templates) Skip bookings flagged by tags, refunds, deposit claims or other negative indicators


Review reminders are scheduled messages that ask the guest to leave a review before the review window closes.[Hospitable's review automation](https://hospitable.com/automate-review-requests) follows up with a guest until they leave a review, and[Airbnb's own guidance](https://www.airbnb.com/resources/hosting-homes/a/why-reviews-matter-41) says that reviewing a guest is one way to remind them to review you. Send the reminder a few days after checkout so it lands inside the window.


Keep automation for smooth stays. Any booking with damage, a broken house rule or an unapproved late checkout needs a review written by a person, so make stopping the automatic review part of your damage process: cancel or edit it in Hostaway, stop it for that reservation in Guesty, tag the booking in OwnerRez, or edit the pending review in Hospitable.


If you would rather hand off review follow-up entirely, Conduit Overwatch, a 24/7 team of AI agents and trained operators, replies to every review in your voice and works to fix a stay that goes wrong before checkout. Plans are on[Conduit's pricing](https://www.conduit.ai/pricing) page.


## FAQ


A host's review of a guest is tied to the reservation, so most edge cases depend on what happened to it. A stay that ended more than 14 days ago is closed to reviews, a booking cancelled before check-in day never opens one, and a group booking puts your review on every confirmed guest's profile.


### Can a host review a guest after 14 days?


A host cannot review an Airbnb guest more than 14 days after checkout, and Airbnb makes no exceptions for late reviews ([Airbnb Help](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/995) ). If something still needs saying after that, send the guest a message or contact Airbnb Support.


### Does my review show up for every guest on the booking?


A host's review of a group appears on the profiles of all confirmed guests who joined the reservation with an Airbnb account, not only the person who booked ([Airbnb Help](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/13) ). Write it with the whole group in mind.


### Can a host review a guest whose reservation was cancelled?


A host cannot review a guest whose reservation was cancelled before the day of check-in. For some reservations cancelled on or after check-in day, counted from 12:00 AM in the listing's time zone, both the host and the guest can still leave a review ([Airbnb Help](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/13) ).


### Should a host review a bad guest or skip the review?


A host should review a guest after a difficult stay, because the review and ratings are what the next host sees. Airbnb's ground rules for guests say hosts can contact Support and leave a review that reflects the experience, and guests who repeatedly break the rules can be suspended or removed ([Airbnb Resource Center](https://www.airbnb.com/resources/hosting-homes/a/ground-rules-for-guests-554) ).


### Can a guest respond to a host's review on Airbnb?


Guests can post a public response directly underneath a host's review on Airbnb ([Airbnb Help](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/32) ). A calm review that sticks to facts from the stay reads better next to the guest's reply than an angry one.


### Does reviewing guests affect Airbnb Superhost status?


Reviewing guests is not a criterion for Airbnb Superhost status. Airbnb checks hosts every quarter against the past 12 months ([Airbnb Help](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/829) ): at least 10 reservations (or 3 reservations totaling 100 nights), a 90% response rate within 24 hours, cancellations below 1%, and a 4.8 or higher overall rating.
